result.title: MetaPOCS: Meta-Learned Multi-Exit Unfolding for Budget-Aware Seismic Data Interpolation
result.summary: Seismic data interpolation must reconcile reconstruction fidelity with the computational budgets of acquisition quality control and subsequent imaging. Fixed-depth unfolding networks are optimized for a single operating point, whereas their intermediate estimates may be insufficiently trained for early deployment. We present MetaPOCS, a meta-learned multi-exit unfolding framework for budget-aware seismic interpolation. Building on a spatial--spectral POCS reconstruction backbone, MetaPOCS supervises intermediate stages and preserves the acquired traces at every exit. A Meta-GF-based optimization procedure constructs exit-oriented parameter displacements from a common initialization and learns their fusion weights through an equal-exit outer objective. The weights vary across parameter tensors and respect the nested support of the reconstruction stages. We derive the resulting fusion hypergradient to characterize how the outer objective reallocates competing updates, and distinguish this mechanism from scalar loss reweighting. At inference, one checkpoint provides a set of reconstruction budgets through a latency-calibrated exit policy. The evaluation framework couples matched-cost interpolation comparisons with finite-update diagnostics and a fixed reverse-time-migration operator, connecting multi-exit optimization to waveform and imaging fidelity. MetaPOCS thus provides a unified formulation for studying the reconstruction--computation trade-off of seismic unfolding across deployment budgets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MetaPOCS：在空间—谱 POCS 展开骨干上构建元学习的多出口结构，监督各中间阶段、学习出口融合权重，并以时延校准的出口策略让单一 checkpoint 支撑多档计算预算的地震数据插值。
